page.layout: One printed page, one column of text running down the page, with the italic passage set within the column. Running head at top, page number at top right. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: castigatur in plurimis locis, Paraphrasis Chaldaica ad antiqua exemplaria M. SS. reformatur, specimen novæ Editionis Bibliorum Antverpiensium correctioris, cui Biblia Pontificia, non verò Regia, nomen futurum erat.

p.i: Hæc Epistola videtur scripta Domino le Jay, cujus sumptibus magna illa Biblia Parisiis edita sunt; nam hoc anno 1628. jam in lucem editum fuerat primum volumen Polyglottorum Parisiensium ex primo volumine Bibliorum Antverpiensium, quæ in hac Epistola vocantur Biblia Regia. Interdum Monachus ille σολοικίξει[?].

main_text.p: ARdentem temporis æstu, febris vexatione, doloribus podagræ invenerunt me literæ Dominationis vestræ; folium Latinis, Græcis, Hebraicisque Hebraice & Chaldaice literis editum inspexi: animum regium in regali sumpto miror: opus mirificum ad conversionem infidelium omnium laudo. Sed advertat Dominatio vestra, vulgatam

page.notes: The initial "A" of the paragraph beginning "ARdentem" is a large woodcut-style initial, transcribed as "A" joined to "Rdentem". The Greek word "σολοικίξει" is printed with ξ where ζ would be expected; kept as printed and marked [?]. The page number is set in old-style figures and read as 135. The italic passage opens with a decorated initial H, transcribed as "Hæc". The top paragraph continues from the previous page. The bottom of the scan is partly shadowed by show-through and a dark stain along the right edge, which was not transcribed.
